clue.text: User of 3 to change pumpkin and modify rag, transforming someone else

indicators.note: transforming tells us the letters of the two words before it are changed into a new order

parts.note: someone else is another person, an other

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale makeover: someone uses magic on a pumpkin and a rag to turn a person into someone new.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' refers to 3-down, the benign magic that in Cinderella turns a pumpkin into a coach. 'transforming' rearranges two clue words into FAIRYGODM; 'someone else' supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Cinderella story it is this magical helper who uses benign sorcery to turn a pumpkin into a carriage.

clue.text: Mark time entertained by ultimate local character in Naxos

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in by them, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Naxos is a Greek island; the Greek letter sigma has a special final form used at the end of a word

explanation.surface: A travel note about leaving one's mark on a Greek island, entertained by a local character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimate local character' sounds like a colourful islander, but it is the Greek letter whose special form ends words, SIGMA; 'entertained by' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace or a visible spot or blemish.

clue.text: Part of set up I used to obstruct bad witch?

definitions.text: Part of set up I used to obstruct bad witch?

indicators.note: to obstruct is to block the way by standing in the middle, so one piece goes inside another
bad signals that the letters of the following word are spoilt into a new order
in a down clue, set up means the piece is written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: in tennis a game is a part of a set

explanation.surface: A spell-book note: the good sort of spell is used to thwart a wicked witch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of set' is tennis: a game is one part of a set. 'up' turns it to EMAG, which with I goes inside WHITC, made by 'bad' from the witch; 'to obstruct' signals the container. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent sorcery, as opposed to the black arts, is what one would use against a malevolent witch.

clue.text: Quip from such as Wellington about extremes of Napoleonism

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: a wellington is a rubber boot, so it is an example of a boot

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, here taken from Napoleonism

explanation.surface: A history quip: the Duke of Wellington making a witty remark about Napoleon's ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wellington' points to the duke who beat Napoleon, but here it is a wellington, the rubber boot; 'about' puts that around the first and last letters picked by 'extremes of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bon mot is French for a witty remark or clever saying.

clue.text: Extremist group minister set up overwhelms current summits

indicators.note: overwhelms means engulfs, so the group surrounds the other piece
in a down clue, set up means the pieces are written from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a sect is a breakaway, often extreme, religious group
Rev is short for Reverend, the title of a minister
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A news line about a radical faction, led by a minister, swamping a series of political summits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns the group and minister together in this down clue, giving VERTCES, which 'overwhelms' the current, so I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vertices are the highest points or apexes, so they are peaks.

clue.text: Sentencing option giving judge trouble

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A courtroom note: a custodial sentence gives the judge some difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Imprisonment is one of the punishments a court can hand down.

clue.text: Set of changes I introduced to fallback, old boy

indicators.note: introduced to means put into, so I goes inside the fallback

parts.note: a fallback is a backup, a Plan B
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Someone describes a backup plan they adapted, introduced to an old schoolfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: In bell-ringing a 'change' is one ordering of the bells; PLAIN BOB is a basic method of ringing them. I goes into PLAN B, then OB follows.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a standard method in English change-ringing, a sequence of permutations rung on church bells.

clue.text: Cook the bacon wrapped around one joint

indicators.note: wrapped around means one piece encloses the other
to cook can mean to falsify or rework, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: cook the bacon wrapped round a joint of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a kitchen verb but rearranges THE BACON, which is 'wrapped around' I for one.
explanation.definitionFit: An aitchbone is a cut of beef from the rump, the buttock bone of cattle.

clue.text: As much as a trace of liquids in short flying?

indicators.note: in means the trace sits inside the other piece
short means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: something flying is aloft, up in the air

indicators.note: a trace of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: An airline question about how much liquid you can take on a short flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short flying' trims ALOFT to ALOF, and L, 'a trace of liquids', goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All of' a quantity means the entire amount, as in 'it cost all of five pounds'.

clue.text: Hard to fire simple sailor boy in uniform

indicators.note: in means the three pieces sit inside the uniform

parts.note: flat can mean uniform, as in a flat rate
mere means simple or nothing more than
a tar is a sailor
Dan is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A story of a simple sailor lad in uniform who is hard to dismiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' suggests clothing but is FLAT, as in a flat rate; 'fire' looks like sacking but is literal burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance described this way resists catching light and slows burning.

clue.text: He's recalled among categorists

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters are read backwards
among says the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: A tribute to a classifier remembered among the great sorters of words.
explanation.walkthrough: The run TEGOR sits inside 'categorists' and 'recalled' reads it backwards. Peter Mark Roget compiled a thesaurus sorted by category, so the clue describes him too.
explanation.definitionFit: Roget's Thesaurus groups words by idea, making its compiler a celebrated classifier of vocabulary.

clue.text: Band of hard rock to teeter metres over missing volume

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for metres

indicators.note: over can mean knocked over or upset, so the letters are rearranged
missing means the volume letter is taken away

parts.note: to teeter is to waver or vacillate

explanation.surface: A gig report about a heavy band nearly toppling from a stage with the sound cut.
explanation.walkthrough: VACILLATE loses V ('missing volume') to leave ACILLATE; with M, 'over' rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Metallica is a famous American heavy metal group.

clue.text: Racial tag abandoned around 2000, following rules on language

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: MM is 2000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A note that a racial label was dropped around the year 2000 under new language rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges RACIAL TAG into GRAATICAL, which goes 'around' MM, the Roman 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: Correct grammar means speech or writing that obeys the conventions of syntax.

clue.text: Turn a load with marks in for treatment here?

definitions.text: Turn a load with marks in for treatment here?

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation is placed inside the rearranged letters
treatment suggests working something over, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A laundry note: spin a load that has stains in it, ready to be cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for treatment' rearranges TURN A LOAD to LAUNDROAT, with M put 'in'. As a whole, the clue pictures a washload with stains being treated at a self-service launderette.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-service launderette is where people bring dirty washing to be cleaned.

clue.text: Extra in Cheers

explanation.surface: A pub note about a bit part in the TV sitcom set in a Boston bar.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball is an extra of this kind; 'cheers' is also casual British for goodbye, shortened to the same word.

clue.text: Beard being cut less, avoiding a cutthroat's edge, could produce this

definitions.text: Beard being cut less, avoiding a cutthroat's edge, could produce this

indicators.note: could produce says the letters before can be reworked to give the answer, once some are taken away
the edge of a word here is its first letter, the leading edge

explanation.surface: A grooming tip: shave less often, skip the cutthroat razor, and you get a fashionable stubbly look.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of BEARD BEING CUT LESS, remove A and C ('avoiding a cutthroat's edge'), and rearrange the rest. The whole clue also says how the look is achieved: shaving less with no razor.
explanation.definitionFit: This deliberately unshaven look of short facial growth is what results from shaving rarely.

clue.text: Loan partner's raised for curriculum

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means lifted upwards, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a sub is a small loan or advance
an ally is a partner, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Someone notes that their partner's loan was raised to pay for a course.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB plus ALLYS gives SUBALLYS, which 'raised' turns over in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllabus lists the topics of a course of study.

clue.text: Might it involve cross in endless crosier waving and mass?

definitions.text: Might it involve cross in endless crosier waving and mass?

indicators.note: in means the cross symbol goes inside the rearranged letters
waving means moving about, so the letters are stirred into a new order
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a cross is drawn as the letter X

explanation.surface: A question about a priest's rite, with a cross, a waving crosier and a mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts CROSIER to CROSIE, 'waving' rearranges it to EORCIS, and X goes 'in'; M follows. The whole clue paints a priest driving out a demon.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving out an evil spirit is a religious rite that may use a cross, a bishop's staff and a mass.

clue.text: Hooter that stings learner driver

parts.note: ow is what one says at a sting of pain
L is the learner driver's plate in the UK

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a horn-honking learner driver is a pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn beside 'learner driver', but it is a bird that hoots. A UK learner driver displays an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: This nocturnal bird is famous for hooting, so it is a hooter.

clue.text: Repressed and excitable types of queen don't make a performance of it!

definitions.text: don't make a performance of it!

parts.note: closet means hidden or repressed, as in a closet fan
a drama queen is someone who overreacts, so this kind of queen gives drama

explanation.surface: Advice to a hidden, overexcitable person: stop making such a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'don't make a performance of it' sounds like 'calm down', but it is literal: a closet drama is a play written to be read, not staged.
explanation.definitionFit: A closet drama is a play meant for reading rather than stage production.

clue.text: Developing green source for yours?

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so the letters of green are rearranged
the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An eco question: is growing a green power supply the solution for your home?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developing' rearranges GREEN into ENERG, and 'source for yours' gives Y. As a whole, the clue asks about green power for your home.
explanation.definitionFit: Green power from renewables is a supply of power for households.

clue.text: Assurance of character actor in a lead

indicators.note: in means the actor goes inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Herbert Lom was a character actor known for the Pink Panther films

explanation.surface: A critic praises a character actor's confidence in a leading role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a leading role, but it is the metal, Pb. Herbert Lom played Inspector Dreyfus in the Pink Panther films.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is calm self-confidence and poise.

clue.text: Feeling distressed? Try facial hair

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
tache is short for moustache

explanation.surface: Advice for the upset: grow a moustache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' looks like 'attempt', but it is the judge's sense of hearing a case. TACHE is British slang for moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional pain or sorrow.

clue.text: Beat finale of rock and roller on heavy metal tracks

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A music note about the drumming that ends a rock-and-roll number from a heavy metal band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock and roller' and 'heavy metal' suggest music, but the roller is an armoured vehicle running on steel tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: An armoured fighting vehicle rolls along on caterpillar treads of steel.

clue.text: Extract of dandelion turns greasy

indicators.note: turns means the letters are read backwards
an extract is a piece taken from inside the word

explanation.surface: A herbal note: dandelion extract becomes greasy.
explanation.walkthrough: DELIO sits inside 'dandelion' and 'turns' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lubricated or covered in lubricant is greasy.

clue.text: Capital of Normandy that succeeds one after dissolution?

definitions.text: Capital of Normandy that succeeds one after dissolution?

indicators.note: that succeeds means the capital letter comes after the other piece

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, one who seeks a dissolute life

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A question about a Norman city that follows on from someone after a period of excess.
explanation.walkthrough: N, the capital letter of 'Normandy', comes after ROUE. The whole clue also names the answer: the chief city of Normandy.
explanation.definitionFit: This city on the Seine is the historic chief city of the Normandy region of France.

clue.text: Expert on points Rushdie informally covers in godless novel's introductions

indicators.note: covers means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: the novelist Salman Rushdie, called by his first name

indicators.note: the introductions of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A literary note: Rushdie writing about introductions in an irreligious novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' suggests a debate, but these are railway points, switches the signal box controls. SALMAN covers IGN, the first letters of 'in godless novel's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker who operates signals and switches is an expert on the track's switching gear.
